title: kac type schema
description: The shape of a type file in `.schema/`. One file declares one record type: its name, its folder, its frontmatter, and what CI checks its records for. A file whose name starts with an underscore, such as `_universal.yaml`, has a shape of its own.

type.description: The singular name of the type, as a record's frontmatter spells it.

label.description: What one record is called in generated prose: "Policy", "ADR", "NFR".

label-plural.description: What a folder of these is called: "Policies", "ADRs", "NFRs". Spell it out, because nothing turns `nfr` into "NFRs".

folder.description: The folder this type's records sit in. This file is named for it, because `kac` reads a document's type from its folder.

page.description: The type's own page, at the corpus root. `kac generate` writes its Metadata and What CI checks blocks.

tier.description: How a document of this type behaves. `_universal.yaml` gives the `tier` field its range, and `_tiers.yaml` says what each value means.

lifecycle.description: How a record ages: `immutable` is superseded, `living` is kept current, `perishable` goes stale until something promotes it.

summary.description: What the type is, in one line. It heads the type's row in the corpus index and renders as a table cell, so `kac` caps it at 120 characters.

goes-here.description: What a contributor has in hand when this type is the answer: "a rule people must follow when building". It fills a cell of the taxonomy's decision table, so `kac` caps it at 120 characters.

detail.description: What the type adds beyond its first sentence, and the edge a reader is most likely to walk over. It renders as a paragraph, so no cell limit applies. Anything true of one corpus alone belongs on the type's own page.

collision.description: Where this type's name already means something else to a reader arriving from another framework. Say what the word means there, and what the reader will get wrong. Separate paragraphs with a blank line and write links inline. Most types collide with nothing and omit this.

versus.description: The calls a contributor could genuinely get wrong, keyed by the other type, rendered as the taxonomy's disambiguation list. Declare a pair once, from the type its heading is titled from: declaring it on both sides fails, and so does declaring one against this type. A pair renders only where the corpus adopted both types.

lineage.description: Where the type's name came from, and where the framework parts company with it. This is the framework's own debt, and it reads the same in every corpus. What one corpus does about an external framework belongs in `frameworks.md`.

prior-art.description: What the type is nearest to, or a statement that nothing established fits. Write links inline, because the generated block cannot see the link definitions at the foot of its page. This is the one required key of `lineage:`, and "none" is a valid answer.

alignment.description: What the framework took from the prior art. A type with no ancestor leaves this and `divergence:` empty, and each renders as an em dash.

divergence.description: Where the framework deliberately parts company.

id.description: How a record of this type is identified.

prefix.description: The part of every id of this type before the hyphen.

style.description: The shape of the id after the hyphen: `numbered` is `width` digits, `mnemonic` is `width` upper-case alphanumerics starting with a letter, `slug` is lower-case words. `kac` checks the shape, then checks it against the discriminator in the filename.

width.description: How many characters a `numbered` or `mnemonic` discriminator takes, as an exact count or a `min`/`max` span. Defaults to 4. A `slug` has no fixed width and ignores this. A span is for `mnemonic` alone, and needs `filename.carries-id: false`, because one filename cannot show several lengths.

min.description: The shortest discriminator this type admits.

max.description: The longest discriminator this type admits.

filename.description: What a record of this type may be called on disk.

pattern.description: What a record's filename must match, `.md` included.

carries-id.description: Whether the filename starts with the id's discriminator, as `0007-decide-x.md` and `vurm-remediation.md` do. Defaults to true. Set it false where records are filed by topic alone, and nothing reads the start of a filename as an id.

slug-max.description: The longest slug a filename may take, in characters. The count drops the extension, and the discriminator where the filename starts with one. Defaults to 30.

fields.description: The frontmatter this type adds to the universal fields, in the order a record writes them. A name `_universal.yaml` also declares refines that universal field.

sections.description: The H2 headings a record of this type has.

required.description: Headings every record must have, each with something written under it. A missing heading fails `required-section`, and a bare one fails `empty-section`.

optional.description: Headings a record may have. One that is present with nothing under it fails `empty-section`.

index.description: The generated table on the type's page.

columns.description: The columns to render, in order. Each is a field the type declares or inherits.

sort.description: The columns to sort on, in order of precedence. Where the first ties, the next decides. Write a scalar for the one-column case. Defaults to `id`, which every document has.

order.description: The direction the whole sort runs in. Defaults to ascending.

parts.description: Where a record of this type keeps the parts something else may cite: what the `.TIMEBOX` of `pol-VURM.TIMEBOX` points at. Omit the block and the type has no parts, so a citation into one of its records resolves to nothing.

source.description: Where the parts are written. `table` reads the rows of the first table under `section:`, each with its own authored id. `headings` reads the headings at `level` under it, each addressed by the anchor the heading slugs to.

section.description: The heading the parts sit under. Must be a section the type declares.

noun.description: What one part is called in the message a citation failure prints: "clause", "term". Defaults to "part".

aside.description: The bold label a part's optional second block starts with: "Not" on a glossary term. An export sends the lead and the aside as two pieces. Omit it where a type's parts have no such block.

level.description: The heading level a part is written at, for `source: headings`. Defaults to 3.

columns.description: The table's headers, in order, for `source: table`. `kac` reads the first two by position as the id and the part, and leaves any further column to the type. Defaults to [Id, Clause].

id-pattern.description: What an authored part id must match: the half after the dot, as in `pol-VURM.TIMEBOX`. Read for `source: table` only, because `kac` derives a heading's id from the heading itself.

binding.description: The modals written bold, which oblige. Declare them strongest first: a record's clause table must group its rows in this order. `source: table` only.

advisory.description: The modals written plain, which recommend. They rank below every binding modal. `source: table` only.

export.description: What a record of this type contributes to a published export, and how much of each piece travels. Once a consumer corpus reads it, the shape is a contract. Omit the block and the type contributes nothing.

version.description: The shape a consumer reads this type's exported files against. Move it by hand where a reader written for the previous shape would now be wrong: a key renamed or dropped, a value whose type changed, a key that means something new. Adding a key moves nothing. Each type has its own.

fields.description: The frontmatter a record contributes, in the order an export writes it. Each is a field the type declares or inherits, or `title`, which is the record's H1. A list travels as a JSON array, and every other value as a string.

sections.description: The sections that travel, keyed by the heading the type declares, each with the fidelity it travels at. A heading the type's `sections:` block does not declare fails.

frameworks.description: The file this type's framework references travel in, relative to the type's own directory. `kac` reads each reference from a clause's `Alignment` cell and writes the lines, so declare the filename and nothing else. Omit it and no references travel.

parts.description: What a record's parts contribute, and the shape of the line each one is written as. `kac` reads them through the type's `parts:` block, so a type exporting parts declares one.

fidelity.description: How much of each part travels. A line is already a reduction, and `line:` below says key by key what a consumer receives.

line.description: The keys one part writes, in order, each with the source that fills it. The key is the type's own word, and a consumer receives it as written.

rules.description: What CI checks a record of this type for, beyond its fields and sections. Reciprocity, section mirroring and conditional requirement are declared on the field, and a rule restating one of them does nothing.

notes.description: Commentary the tool never reads. Allowed at every level and required at none. Where a field declares both, the type page shows `description:`, and `notes:` keeps the reasoning local to that field in one paragraph. A field with only `notes:` renders those. Put an argument longer than a paragraph on the design site.

regex.description: A .NET regular expression, anchored, and quoted in YAML so the backslashes survive.

fidelity.description: How much of one piece travels into an export. `full` sends it whole, `summary` cuts it to its opening block, and `reference` sends the key and none of its words. Write it against every entry, because there is no default.

lineSource.description: Where one key of a part line takes its value from. `part.lead` and `part.aside` read a part's body, which only a `source: headings` type gives a part. A `source: table` type sends the row through `part.text` and its columns. `front.<field>` is a field the type declares or inherits, and `column.<Header>` is a header its `parts.columns:` declares.

field.description: One frontmatter key, and everything asked of its value.

description.description: What a reader needs at a glance, in one line. It renders into the generated Metadata table, which pads every column to its widest cell, so keep it under about 100 characters and leave the reasoning to `notes:`. An enum's `values:` sit outside that budget, because they render in a small table of their own beneath.

required.description: Whether every record must write the key.

required-when.description: The condition under which an otherwise optional field must be filled in, as one test against one other field of the same document. Three forms and no others: `other == value`, `other != value`, `other in [a, b]`. Where the other field is absent the condition is false, `!=` included.

type.description: What the value is. Defaults to `string`. A `date` is one day, written quoted. A `timestamp` is a moment in UTC, written unquoted as `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ`. An `object` is one mapping, and `entry:` or `shape:` declares its keys.

of.description: What each entry of a list is. `object` makes each entry a mapping, and `entry:` declares its keys.

entry.description: The keys of one object, declared where `type: object` or `of: object` makes a value one. Each key takes the same `type:`, `pattern:` and `required:` a field does. The first key declared identifies the entry: `list-order` sorts on it, and an index column renders it.

shape.description: A shared object shape from `_shapes.yaml`, taken whole in place of an `entry:` block. A shape cannot be narrowed where it is used, so a type needing a tighter value on one of its keys writes a rule with an `expr:`.

values.description: An enum's range. Write it inline, draw it from `_enums.yaml` as `$enums.<name>`, or leave it to the corpus as `$corpus.<name>`, which reads `enums:` in `.corpus.yaml`.

ref.description: The folders an id in this field may point into. Write a scalar for the one-folder case. `kac` checks both halves: that the id resolves to a record, and that the record is one of these types. A folder this corpus declined goes unchecked, and adopting that type starts the check with no edit here.

part-required.description: Whether an id in this field must point at a part of a record and never at the whole record. A standard's `implements:` declares it, and cites clauses one by one. A `mirrors-citations:` line is held to it too. Needs a `ref:` to resolve the part against, and every type that `ref:` lists must declare parts.

reciprocal.description: The field on the target record that must point back. `kac` resolves every id against the corpus anyway, so this adds the return leg and nothing else.

pattern.description: A further constraint on the value, applied to each entry where the field is a list.

from.description: Where the field's value comes from, for a field the record never writes. `sub-path` is the folders between the type's own folder and the file, so `standards/platform/node/testing.md` gets `platform/node`. A record filed straight into its type folder gets an empty value. A derived field may not also be `required:`.

mirrors-section.description: The section whose ids this field must mirror, which must be one the type's `sections:` block declares. `kac` compares the field against the section in both directions and case-insensitively, reading ids from a bullet or from prose. The field must list everything the section cites.

mirrors-citations.description: The label on the footnote lines whose citations this field must mirror. Each line closes the section it gathers, written in italic with the label bold: `_**Covers:** [pol-SCRT].EMBED_`. The ids across every line must equal the field, compared in both directions and case-insensitively. A section covering nothing gets no line, and a malformed line is reported where it sits. Needs a `ref:`.

allow-literal.description: Words admitted beside the field's declared type: `last-rehearsed: never`, `applies-to: [all]`. `kac` takes a value listed here as written. On a list the exemption applies to the entry, so the ids beside it are still checked as ids.

min-items.description: The shortest a list may be, for a field whose value is its breadth. Only a `type: list` field may declare it.

min-records.description: The fewest records that may share one value, for a field whose values group documents. `kac` counts per type, case-insensitively, and once per record however often it repeats a value. It warns on every record using a value below the floor, and never errors.

rule.description: One entry of a type's `rules:` block. A rule states an intention from the moment it is written, and gains a `severity:` once something can run it.

id.description: What runs the rule: the `expr:` below, or a rule class registered under this same name.

description.description: What is checked, in one line. It renders into the type page's checks table, so `kac` caps it at 120 characters. The diagnosis belongs in `message:`.

severity.description: Whether tripping the rule fails a build or advises an author. Leave it out for a rule nothing runs yet, and the type page renders the rule as declared and unenforced.

expr.description: The condition a document must satisfy. A rule declaring one needs no C#. Leave it out where the check needs a real algorithm, and where nothing runs the rule yet.

message.description: What the author is told when the expression fails. Say what is wrong, then what to write instead.

postures.description: The framework standings a roll-up rule checks a policy's `aligns-with` against, spelled as the corpus's own framework register heads them. A clause may still cite a framework filed under another standing, and that framework stays out of the roll-up.

max-words.description: The most words a Y-statement may take.
